title: Contrastive Conceptor Activation Steering (COAST): Unlocking Vision-Language-Action Models through Hidden States
venue: arXiv preprint (included.json lists ICML 2026 Workshop on Mechanistic Interpretability)
models: pi0.5 (MetaWorld, LIBERO, RoboCasa; pi0.5-DROID on real robot)
action_head: mixed: flow/diffusion action expert (pi0.5, GR00T N1.5), discrete action tokens (pi0-FAST), diffusion policy (DP)
methods: Boolean conceptor algebra C+ AND NOT C-
question: Can a closed-form subspace gate fit from a handful of success and failure rollouts, applied to the action expert's residual stream, raise task success of frozen robot policies?
key_findings: LIBERO-10: pi0.5 mean success 0.43 -> 0.80 with per-step COAST (+0.37, p<.001); pi0-FAST 0.62 -> 0.84 (+0.23); CAA gives +0.04 and SFT on the same 15 rollouts -0.03 for pi0.5 (Table 1).
MetaWorld ML45 (10 tasks shown in Table 1): pi0.5 0.69 -> 0.94 (+0.25); pi0-FAST 0.71 -> 0.82 (+0.11). The main text gives different numbers for the same comparison (0.57 -> 0.82 and 0.57 -> 0.69).

RoboCasa (7 tasks): pi0.5 0.40 -> 0.55-0.56 (+0.15 to +0.16); GR00T N1.5 0.59 -> 0.75 (+0.16, pz=.006); Diffusion Policy 0.32 -> 0.46 (+0.14, per-step); for DP the pooled z-test gives p = .058 for global and .289 for positive-only, so the text's 'all strategies remain significant' does not hold for DP (as parsed from Table 1).

Real robot (DROID Franka, pi0.5-DROID, 3 tasks x 15 trials): reported 40% average improvement; figure values read as Open Drawer 0.33 -> 0.86, Close Microwave 0.06 -> 0.46, Put Duck 0.13 -> 0.40 (pi0-FAST and GR00T lower; numbers reconstructed from garbled figure text).
Contrastive (global / per-step) beats positive-only steering, and per-step helps more on long-horizon tasks; gains are larger when baseline success is low.
Contrastive subspace is low-rank but not rank-one (about 1% of the 1024-dim pi0.5 expert); per-task gain correlates with success/failure conceptor overlap (Spearman rho = 0.59, p = 0.002, MetaWorld).

Failure geometry is shared across tasks while success geometry is task-specific: failure-subspace containment predicts cross-task transfer gain (r = 0.30, p = 4.5e-3 LIBERO; r = 0.49, p = 1.1e-3 RoboCasa), success containment does not (|r| < 0.13).

Best layer clusters at 11 of 18 for the pi0.5 expert and 10 of 16 for the GR00T DiT; beta in {0.1, 0.3} best in over 90% of cells; geometric hyperparameter selection recovers about 93% of oracle success using 3-8% of the grid.

evidence.setting: both (three simulation benchmarks plus 3 real DROID tasks)
benchmarks: real DROID: Open Drawer, Close Microwave, Put Duck in Cabinet
evidence.scale: 15 fitting rollouts per task (conceptor fit + hyperparameter selection) and 30 held-out test rollouts per task per condition with disjoint seeds; real robot 15 trials per task. No training-seed replication.
evidence.statistics: yes for simulation: paired t-test across tasks and pooled two-proportion z-test per model-benchmark; no CIs; real-robot results without tests
evidence.baselines: unsteered policy, CAA (single-direction mean-difference addition), TopK SAE feature steering (Khan et al. 2025), LoRA SFT on the same 15 rollouts; CAA/SAE strengths picked post hoc on the evaluation set (favouring those baselines)

causal_validation: Yes, the intervention itself is causal: gating the action-expert residual stream changes closed-loop success, and positive-only vs contrastive variants act as an ablation of the failure-subtraction term. The geometric claims (low rank, overlap, shared failure structure) are correlational analyses of the fitted conceptors, not separately intervened on.
closed_loop: Yes, all success rates are closed-loop rollouts in simulation and on the real robot.
limitations_stated: Requires both success and failure rollouts; uniformly successful tasks fall back to positive-only steering.
Tasks with nearly disjoint success/failure subspaces show smaller gains.
Unclear whether geometric hyperparameter selection generalizes beyond tested architectures.
Steering is hard to detect from action traces and could be misused to steer toward failure; recommend logging conceptors.
critique: Simulation baselines are deliberately weak 'early fine-tuning checkpoints' on MetaWorld and LIBERO, chosen to produce failures; large gains over undertrained policies say little about steering a fully trained model.
Main text and Table 1 disagree on MetaWorld means (0.57 -> 0.82 vs 0.69 -> 0.94), which lowers confidence in the reporting.

Success-labelled rollouts in the target task are needed, so COAST is closer to few-shot test-time adaptation using outcome labels than to interpretability; the 'action expert is the bottleneck' hypothesis is not directly tested (no comparison with steering the VLM backbone at matched budget, and pi0-FAST has no separate expert).
Real-robot claim rests on 15 trials per task, one checkpoint, no statistical test, and an unclear number of fitting rollouts ('a single successful rollout' for Close Microwave).
30 test rollouts per task make per-task differences noisy; the paper reports the best of three strategies per row, which adds a mild selection effect.
One of the few steering papers to cover flow-matching, token and diffusion heads in one protocol, and the comparison with CAA, SAE steering and SFT at equal data is useful.
one_line: Fitting conceptor subspaces from 15 success/failure rollouts and softly projecting the action expert's hidden states onto the success-not-failure subspace raises closed-loop success for pi0.5, pi0-FAST, GR00T and Diffusion Policy in simulation and on a real DROID arm.
